_comment: Mutation spec for the four measurement instruments: M9 fidelity, M10 caption alignment,
M11 A/V sync, M12 pairwise preference.
A broken instrument is worse than no instrument, and the reason is specific to this spec: a
wrong measurement does not look wrong. It looks like a finding. Every mutation below produces
a number that is plausible, publishable, and about nothing -- which is exactly the shape of
the defect the whole `evaluation/` package exists to prevent.
The highest-value ones, per the spec's task 7.4:
mean_where_minimum_required  -- hides the single worst frame, which is the one a viewer sees
invert_degradation           -- a worse encode scores better; every future comparison inverts
absolute_alignment_error     -- destroys the lag/jitter distinction, the metric's only use
skip_alignment_check         -- compares frame N against N+1 and reports it as fidelity loss
drop_declines                -- manufactures a preference out of 'nobody could tell'
Note the command runs all four instruments' tests together. They share no code, but they do
share a failure mode -- an instrument agreeing with itself -- and running them as one batch

mutations.name: mean_where_minimum_required
mutations.why: R1.8's exact failure. The minimum becomes the mean, so the single worst frame disappears -- and a mean SSIM of 0.98 is entirely compatible with one frame at 0.4, which is what a scene-change encode decision produces and what a viewer notices. Both fields still look like measurements.

mutations.name: minimum_and_mean_swapped
mutations.why: Adjacent fields, same type, both plausible. Swapping them makes every reading look slightly better than it is, which is the direction nobody questions.

mutations.name: invert_degradation
mutations.why: A worse encode scores better. Every comparison made with this instrument from now on points the wrong way, and a self-comparison alone cannot catch it -- which is precisely why task 2.6 exists as a separate test from 2.5.

mutations.name: ssim_summary_line_counted_as_a_frame
mutations.why: The bug this module actually shipped with for an hour. ffmpeg prints an `ssim` summary line containing `All:`, so a bare pattern reports 51 readings for a 50-frame file and folds the summary into the mean. The self-comparison identity test does NOT catch it -- on identical input the summary is also 1.0. Only the cross-parser frame-count assertion does.

mutations.name: skip_alignment_check
mutations.why: R1.6. ffmpeg happily compares frame N against N+1 for the whole remainder and returns a number that is plausible, terrible and about nothing. Somebody then acts on it. A refusal is worth more than any reading here.

mutations.name: alignment_check_ignores_frame_count
mutations.why: Keeps the resolution guard -- the one that would have errored inside ffmpeg anyway -- and drops the frame-count guard, which is the half that silently misaligns. The more tempting mutation of the two, because it still looks like a guard.

mutations.name: absent_libvmaf_as_pass
mutations.why: R1.5, R7.9. 'Could not measure' becomes 'nothing wrong' for any caller doing `report.get(metric, ok)`, because the key is simply absent. Three distinguishable states collapse into two.

mutations.name: compare_across_ffmpeg_builds
mutations.why: R2.6/R2.7. The arithmetic works perfectly, which is the problem: differencing two builds yields a filter-implementation or libvmaf-model change dressed as a fidelity finding.

mutations.name: absolute_alignment_error
mutations.why: R3.3, and the single most valuable mutation in this file. A constant +150 ms lag and symmetric +/-150 ms jitter give identical absolute statistics and need completely different fixes -- one constant compensation versus forced alignment. Every summary number still looks reasonable.

mutations.name: unmatched_events_dropped
mutations.why: R3.7. Exactly how a metric improves while the output gets worse: match three events of forty, report a beautiful 2 ms mean, and the count that would have revealed it is gone.

mutations.name: caption_timing_measures_the_word_list_not_the_render
mutations.why: R3.4 in miniature: leaving `{\kf80}` override blocks in the text breaks token matching for eleven of the fourteen caption presets, so the karaoke styles silently stop being measured at all while the non-karaoke ones keep reporting.

mutations.name: rounding_floor_forgotten
mutations.why: `_ass_timestamp` rounds to centiseconds, so +/-5 ms is the format rather than drift. A zero floor invites someone to spend an afternoon chasing 3 ms.

mutations.name: sync_offset_unsigned
mutations.why: Audio late and audio early are different defects with different causes. Unsigned, they are the same reading.

mutations.name: sync_silence_reported_as_synchronised
mutations.old:
if peak == 0:
        raise SyncError(f"audio in {path} is silent; no event to locate")
mutations.why: The failure that reads as perfect sync. A silent file has no locatable event, and returning 0.0 turns 'I could not measure this' into a number indistinguishable from success.

mutations.name: sync_flash_threshold_removed
mutations.why: Symmetric to the above: with no flash present the brightest frame is frame 0, so a missing visual event is silently located at t=0 and every offset becomes the audio onset.

mutations.name: drop_declines
mutations.why: R5.4. Manufactures a preference out of 'nobody could tell', which for a change costing render time is the most useful finding available and the one most convenient to lose.

mutations.name: randomise_per_set_instead_of_per_trial
mutations.why: R5.3. Every baseline lands in slot A, so a judge who mildly prefers the left-hand video reads as preferring the baseline. Still 'randomised' if you only inspect one trial, and the reason Property 1 is a property test rather than an example.

mutations.name: tally_counts_slots_not_configurations
mutations.old: chosen = trial.config_a if judgement.choice == CHOICE_A else trial.config_b
mutations.new: chosen = preference_set.baseline if judgement.choice == CHOICE_A else preference_set.candidate
mutations.why: Defeats the blinding entirely by resolving 'the left one' to a fixed configuration. With order randomised, the result is noise reported as a preference -- and the counts still add up.

mutations.name: blinding_leaked_into_the_presented_view
mutations.why: R5.2. Puts the answer key in the file the judge opens. Knowing which render is 'the new one' produces the expected answer, and nothing downstream can detect that it happened.

mutations.name: significance_claim_introduced
mutations.old:
" This is a directional signal, not a measurement:"
        " a trial count this small cannot distinguish a real preference from noise,"
        " and no significance test is applied or implied."
mutations.why: R5.5, R5.6. With a handful of trials and usually one judge -- often the author of the change -- this is false precision dressed as rigour. The mutation is trivial to write and would be quoted in a PR.
